steps.name: branch name
steps.why: Conventional Branch: <type>/<description>. In CI it reads the PR's head branch, so --no-verify does not get past it. Bot branches pass.

steps.name: unit (changed)
steps.why: Only the tests the diff reaches, so the push stays inside the budget. The full suite runs in CI.

steps.name: workflow guards
steps.why: Tests for the run guards: guard-workflow.mjs (Claude hook) and check-pr-workflow.mjs (PR gate). Plain node:test, no vitest needed.

steps.name: pr workflow
steps.why: Issue link, Decision line that names an existing Decision in the Concept database (CONCEPT_DATABASE_URL), tests with source changes. Reads the PR body, so it runs in CI only; elsewhere it passes.

steps.name: storybook build
steps.why: The design system's Storybook deploys from main to its own Vercel project. A story that does not build must fail here, not there.

steps.name: lint styles
steps.why: Only Carbon tokens in src/design-system. stylelint fails on a raw colour and a raw size.

steps.name: audit
steps.why: High and critical advisories only. Lower levels fire on transitive dev dependencies and train everyone to ignore the check.

steps.name: e2e smoke
steps.why: A merge gate needs the critical paths, not the suite. Tag those specs @smoke; the rest runs nightly.

steps.name: deps drift
steps.why: Reports, never fails: npm outdated exits 1 whenever anything is behind, which is always.

steps.name: security scan
steps.why: Semgrep Community Edition ships on PyPI, not npm, so the runner needs python and pipx. --error turns findings into a non-zero exit. --exclude .agents skips skills that skilly vendors: the consumer cannot fix them, sync overwrites them. --exclude keeps Semgrep's default ignore list, a .semgrepignore would replace it.
